payload.headline: Amazon jumps 3.82% to 267.74, above its value range; still waiting

summary.thesis: Margins are improving, but slower sales growth, $46.9B of cash burn over the last year and a price above its own value range leave no margin of safety.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: no trade, because the price sits just under resistance with little room to run.
summary.act_at: Buy near 238.65; no new buying above 265.96

payload.happening: Amazon rose 3.82% to 267.74. That moved the price above the top of its own-history value range (265.96) and just above its nearest support zone (263.7–267.56). TechCrunch reported that Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO. No earnings date appears in the data.
payload.business: Three things change the business itself. First, sales growth is slowing: the latest quarter grew 12.09% from a year earlier, down from 16.61% two quarters earlier. Second, profitability is improving: operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. A filing risk note says that 13% is the top of its 5-year range, and margins at a peak tend to fade. Third, cash is going the wrong way. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and investing) was -46.9B over the last 12 months, against 10.6B a year earlier. Net debt (debt minus cash) is 66.7B. Unpaid customer bills rose 61%, while sales rose 12%. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. The Anthropic report mainly changes how investors feel about the stock and what Amazon's stake could be worth. It does not change Amazon's sales, margins or cash today. (General knowledge: Anthropic is also a cloud customer, so the tie-up may matter to AWS over time, but the data has no figures on this.) Not at risk: liquidity (cash plus available credit) is 114.2B, and dilution (new shares diluting existing owners) was only 0.77% over the year. At risk: the cash burn, and whether growth keeps slowing.

worth.text: A discounted cash flow model (which values a company by its future cash) is not possible here, because free cash flow is negative. That leaves price-to-sales, the price compared with each dollar of yearly sales. Amazon trades at 3.6 times sales, which is the 70th percentile of its own 5-year history. Using its own history, fair value runs from 187.93 to 265.96, with a middle of 238.65. The price of 267.74 is above even the top of that range. Against peers, Amazon looks cheaper: the peer median is 6.6 times sales, and after adjusting for growth Amazon sits at 0.6 versus peers. The gap between the two methods comes down to one question: is Amazon a retailer-like business valued on its own history, or a tech platform valued like its peers? On earnings, the price is 21.7 times trailing earnings and 25.1 times next year's estimate. Analysts expect next year's earnings per share (10.67) to come in below this year's (12.8). A filing risk note says the price needs about 34% a year of growth, while the company delivered 13% a year over 3 years.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.6.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now produces more profit.
Adjusted for growth, Amazon is valued at 0.6 versus peers, and its price-to-sales of 3.6 is well below the peer median of 6.6.
Analysts raised next year's earnings estimate by 1.4% over 30 days, and Amazon and Google were reported to jointly own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B over 12 months from 10.6B a year earlier, and net debt is 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters earlier, while unpaid customer bills rose 61%.
At 267.74 the price is above the 265.96 top of its value range, and a filing risk note says it needs about 34% a year of growth versus 13% delivered.

levels.what: Top of the own-history value range. No buying above it, and the price is above it now.
The 200-day average. A small first entry here only if the next filing shows free cash flow better than -46.9B.
Middle of the own-history value range, where price meets fair value. This is the main buy level.

longterm.why: Better margins do not yet outweigh slowing growth and cash burn, and today's jump put the price above the top of the value range. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: The price sits right at the top of support (263.7–267.56) and below resistance at 274.75. That gap is smaller than one typical day's move (the ATR, or average daily range, is 9.02), so the possible gain is too small for the risk. All three averages (20-, 50- and 200-day) are flat, and the macro view is a tech downtrend, so there is no clean setup.

decision.timing: No earnings date is in the data, so the next decision points depend on price: a pullback to 244.91, or a close above 278.56. Options to 2026-12-18 price in a move of about 8.8%, with implied volatility (47.4) above recent actual volatility (42.4).

change_mind: The next filing shows free cash flow better than -46.9B and quarterly sales growth back above 16.61%. That would justify buying above 244.91.
A close above the resistance top of 278.56 would show a break out of the range and would change the swing view from 'no trade' to looking for an entry.
A close below the support zone bottom of 258.08 would bring the 238.65 buy level closer and confirm the rejection of today's jump.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: the decision is still wait, and today's 3.82% jump to 267.74 confirmed it by pushing the price above the 265.96 top of the value range.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
